_comment: What a delivery team can actually get today: a bundle of standard, reference architecture, modules and templates, with someone operating it. `enables` names the capabilities it gives tooling for; `assets` are ids in facts/assets.json; `in_the_box` is the control checklist the platform team answers. Released counts are derived from asset statuses by build/facts.py, not stored here. `was` records the realization ids this offering was migrated from on 4 September 2026; `note` is the migration note and may still use the superseded readiness vocabulary.

generic_assets.name: Published standard
generic_assets.why: The institutional standard for how this is built.

generic_assets.name: Architecture pattern document
generic_assets.why: Problem, context, forces, solution, resulting context - not just a name.

generic_assets.name: CI/CD pipeline
generic_assets.why: Change is built and released through a controlled path.

generic_assets.name: Security baseline
generic_assets.why: Identity, network and data controls applied by default.

generic_assets.name: Observability wired
generic_assets.why: Telemetry emitted without the team adding it.

generic_assets.name: Runbook
generic_assets.why: Operations know what to do when it misbehaves.

consumption_models.name: Guidance
consumption_models.definition: EA tells you how to build it.

consumption_models.name: Building blocks
consumption_models.definition: Reusable modules and components are provided.

consumption_models.name: Reference implementation
consumption_models.definition: A working implementation exists and can be adapted.

consumption_models.name: Managed platform
consumption_models.definition: The platform provides the underlying infrastructure; the consumer configures on top.

consumption_models.name: Service / API
consumption_models.definition: The consumer calls it and gets a result.

offerings.name: Foundry platform
offerings.operated_by: Consumer - each team deploys and runs its own instance
offerings.note: REAL-001: Standard published, reference architecture published, both Terraform modules published in JFrog. This is the strongest realization in the estate.

offerings.name: Foundry agents
offerings.operated_by: Consumer - each team deploys and runs its own instance
offerings.not_provided: The agent itself: business rules, grounding data, evaluation criteria, human oversight design. Those remain with the delivery team.

in_the_box.control: Distinct workload identity per instance, not a shared service principal
in_the_box.why: A shared service principal makes every agent's actions indistinguishable. Nothing downstream can attribute or revoke.

in_the_box.control: Automatic registration in the AI system / agent inventory
in_the_box.why: An inventory that depends on teams remembering to register is not an inventory.

in_the_box.control: Tracing and tool-call logging enabled by default
in_the_box.why: If it is not on by default it will not be there when you need to explain what an agent did.

in_the_box.control: Content filtering and safety controls on by default
in_the_box.why: Opt-in safety is the control that is missing exactly when it is needed.

in_the_box.control: Prompt-injection defence configured
in_the_box.why: Content the agent reads can instruct it. Prompt design alone does not stop this at run time.

in_the_box.control: Evaluation harness scaffolded in the template
in_the_box.why: Without a harness in the template, evaluation happens once at launch and never again.

in_the_box.control: Cost attribution tags applied automatically
in_the_box.why: Untagged consumption cannot be attributed, forecast or stopped.

in_the_box.control: A tested way to stop it and revoke its access
in_the_box.why: An untested kill switch is an assumption, not a control.

in_the_box.control: Credential issuance and rotation handled by the platform
in_the_box.why: Credentials created by hand are credentials nobody rotates.

in_the_box.control: Network isolation and private connectivity baseline
in_the_box.why: Isolation applied per team is isolation applied inconsistently.

in_the_box.control: A hook for human approval of consequential actions
in_the_box.why: Oversight designed into the platform is exercised; oversight written into policy is not.

in_the_box.control: Interaction log retention configured to policy
in_the_box.why: Interaction logs are evidence. Retention set per project is evidence you cannot rely on.

offerings.note: REAL-002: READINESS 3, NOT 4 - and only because the documentation trails the engineering. The Terraform modules are published and in use; the Foundry Agents Standard (STD-07) and its Reference Architecture (RA-05) are both PRE-RELEASE. Releasing those two documents is the whole distance to 4. Confirm this reading.

offerings.name: Custom MCP servers
offerings.operated_by: Consumer - each team deploys and runs its own server

in_the_box.control: Server registered in an approved-server registry before any client may call it
in_the_box.why: A public registry entry is not enterprise approval. Discovery and approval are different registers.

in_the_box.control: Acting user's identity propagated on-behalf-of to the system of record
in_the_box.why: Without it every action looks like the service account and the audit trail names the wrong actor.

in_the_box.control: Tool scopes issued at least privilege
in_the_box.why: A tool that can do more than its purpose is the confused-deputy path.

in_the_box.control: Traffic passes a gateway or policy enforcement point
in_the_box.why: Per-server enforcement is enforcement that varies by team.

in_the_box.control: Protocol revision pinned, with a migration plan for the July 2026 spec
in_the_box.why: Roots, Sampling, Logging, RFC 7591 dynamic client registration and legacy HTTP+SSE are deprecated on defined timelines. Template v1 predates this.

in_the_box.control: Tool calls audited with arguments and effect
in_the_box.why: You cannot explain what an agent did without the call record.

offerings.note: REAL-003: Standard, reference architecture and a working template that built every custom MCP server on the AI MVP project. TEMPLATE v1 IMPLEMENTS THE SUPERSEDED MCP SPECIFICATION - the July 2026 revision deprecated Roots, Sampling, Logging, RFC 7591 dynamic client registration and the legacy HTTP+SSE transport on defined timelines. Every server built from v1 needs a migration plan inside that window, and v2 is built but not yet distributed. That is a dated roadmap item, not a maturity opinion.

offerings.name: Retrieval on AI Search

in_the_box.control: Entitlement enforced at query time, before ranking
in_the_box.why: Filtering a ranked list after the fact both leaks and distorts relevance. The filter must precede ranking.

in_the_box.control: Citations resolvable to source, version and location
in_the_box.why: A citation that cannot be opened is decoration. It also does not prove the statement is true.

in_the_box.control: Retrieval quality measured against a benchmark
in_the_box.why: Relevance that is never measured degrades silently as the corpus changes.

in_the_box.control: Re-embedding runbook for model change
in_the_box.why: Changing the embedding model invalidates the index. Without a runbook this is an outage.

in_the_box.control: Index residency and access controls enforced
in_the_box.why: A vector index is a copy of the source content, and inherits its residency obligations.

offerings.note: REAL-004: Standard, reference architecture and a published Terraform module. Supply is well packaged - which is exactly why the maturity of capability 3.6 must be argued separately. See REAL-005. | REAL-005: CONFIRM THIS ROW - it decides the headline finding for D3. Does the Azure AI Search Standard (STD-04) mandate that source ACL metadata is extracted, indexed and applied as a pre-ranking filter? If it does, readiness follows REAL-004. If it does not, this sits at 0 and it is the reason capability 3.6 can carry readiness 4 and a much lower maturity. Filtering a ranked list after the fact both leaks and distorts relevance.

offerings.name: Document extraction

in_the_box.control: Extraction confidence thresholds set and enforced
in_the_box.why: Extraction without a confidence floor silently promotes guesses to facts.

in_the_box.control: Human validation path for low-confidence output
in_the_box.why: The threshold is only useful if something happens when it is not met.

in_the_box.control: Page and bounding-box provenance retained
in_the_box.why: An extracted value that cannot be traced to a page is unverifiable downstream.

in_the_box.control: Output validated against a declared schema
in_the_box.why: Schema validation is what makes the output machine-consumable rather than plausible text.

offerings.note: REAL-006: Standard and reference architecture published; no Terraform module in the inventory. Publishing one is the step to 4.

offerings.name: Approved AI tech stack
offerings.note: REAL-007: The approved AI technology stack. This is the asset that answers 'what is already approved for general use' at the technology level - it is evidence toward capability maturity, not a substitute for it.

offerings.name: Agent design guidance
offerings.note: REAL-008: A published decision aid for whether and what kind of agent is appropriate. This is the only realization currently touching domain D2, and it maps to the autonomy and interaction-pattern determination.
